description:
Symptom: a program that reduces over records read through File.stream!/Stream.map/JSON.decode! finishes compiling and fails in materialization with "public closure callsite N settled return X disagrees with its semantic result type Y" or "missing semantic result type for public closure callsite N". Every finishing cut of tools/distill-telemetry.exs ends here.

Minimal programs (fz-xxd13-build session scratchpad s133/, verified on 3038a76af):
- min.fz (oracle min.exs prints 0), ~1.1 s compile, "disagrees" form:
    rs = Enum.to_list(Stream.map([1], fn _ -> JSON.decode!("{}") end))
    IO.inspect(Enum.reduce(rs, 0, fn r, acc -> Enum.reduce(r, acc, fn _, a -> a end) end))
- min_missing.fz, "missing" form:
    rs = Enum.to_list(Stream.map([1], fn _ -> JSON.decode!("{}") end))
    for r <- rs, into: [], do: Enum.map(r, fn x -> x end)
The inner receiver must be an any-typed list element; a literal source list compiles.

Cause (verified by probes unless marked):
- The callsite is reducer.(head, acc) in List.reduce_cont/3 (lib/list.fz:111). The diagnostic is raised only in public_indirect_return_ty (jobs/artifact.rs), which compares CallSiteSummary.return_ty with analysis.value_types[result].
- jobs/semantic.rs analyzes each activation input row separately. A row whose callee is a bare fun returns unresolved(Known(any)); deliver_call_return unions that any into value_types, which is rebuilt each pass. The summary is built by merge_call_emission, whose (_, Unresolved) arm drops that row, and CallSiteMap::define joins the summary's return across rounds. So the value type is a per-pass rebuild and the summary a cross-round join; nothing makes them one fact. In min.fz the semantic any is the honest half and the summary is wrong.
- "missing" form: the row's callee is fun | closure(..) | closure(..) with type variables in the closures; callable_value_clauses yields nothing, has_vars makes it "not a dynamic edge", and the answer is Bottom for good (the last step inferred from the code path and the printed row).
- The bare fun arrives because an any receiver reaches the Stream implementation, which dispatches on its own enum: any again and nests Stream.compose closures until the nesting ends as fun (the widening cut itself was not instrumented).

Spikes so far (evidence only): joining the dynamic row's any into the summary (s133/spike.patch) cures min.fz on interp, run and build with lib 2169/0, but flips the disagreement on min2.fz and R4 and leaves the "missing" form. Letting the callable top absorb the other function clauses at intern (s133/fun_absorbs_spike.patch, the fz-sc8.130 shape) only moves the errors.

Fix shape under spike: one fact. The callsite summary's return joins every row's return, the call result's value type is read from the stored summary, and the artifact check has nothing left to compare. fz-sc8.131 (closure_elem.fz) is a different cause: it fails in backend lowering on delivered lanes and is unchanged by the spike.

comments.text: 2026-11-13 grid on 549fd7447 (develop + .140 + .147 + .131), interp, binaries in scratchpad grid/: OptionParser's library spike S1 (nested stream flattened) alone makes s133/min.fz, min_missing.fz, x2.fz, the sfor/ for/reduce programs, R4, M1, n1, anat/min.fz and min_plus_site compile and match; the one-fact spike alone leaves the for/reduce programs at 'Enumerable.reduce/3 has no implementation' (the any of the bare-fun row widens Enum.to_list to any and drives one lambda with {any, any} and int | float); both together equal S1 alone. Recommendation withdrawn: this ticket waits for fz-sc8.127 and should follow its per-row design; it may be unnecessary once fun rows are not manufactured. The missing/no-implementation forms are the same root (sfor/ investigation), not separate bugs.

title: A public closure callsite's settled return agrees with its semantic result
